description.narrative:
Sport for Sustainable Urban Development Initiative is an initiative being seeded by UN-Habitat and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to contribute to realising the potential of sport, physical activity and active recreation as an important enabler of sustainable development at scale in cities and urban environments. The overall aim is to contribute to creating more inclusive, healthier, environmentally friendly urban societies. The initiative focuses on mainstreaming sport, physical activity and active recreation in UN Habitat’s SDG Cities and Inclusive Communities, Thriving Cities initiatives, and in doing so, contribute to the focus of Olympic Agenda 2020+5 and the IOC’s Olympism365 strategy centred on the role of sport as a tool for inclusive sustainable development. SDG Cities and Inclusive Communities, Thriving Cities provides a systematic global approach to accelerate the achievement of SDGs in cities and urban areas through collaborative action. The Sport for Sustainable Urban Development Initiative has a particular focus on utilising sport, physical activity and active recreation as a catalyst to accelerate the achievement of the SDGs, for example SDG 3 focused on good health and wellbeing, SDG 11 on making cities and human settlements inclusive, safe and resilient, and SDG 10 on reducing inequalities within and among countries. Rationale The rationale and value proposition of the initiative draws on recognition of the importance of cities and urban communities in achieving the SDGs along with evidence of the social and economic outcomes that can be delivered through sport-based policies and investment. With the percentage of the world’s population accommodated in cities and urban areas set to grow from 55% to 70% by 2050, it is widely recognised that achieving the SDGs has a strong urban dimension. UN Habitat’s SDG Cities and Inclusive Communities, Thriving Cities provide a systematic approach to deliver on this dimension through providing a framework for improved data collection and analysis; strategic planning; the strengthening of local institutions; and the financing and implementation of high impact projects in cities and urban environments. Moreover, this project is not only a collaboration between FP1 -Inclusive Communities, Thriving Cities, FP5 SDG Cities and the wider SDG Localization offering, but teams within the Planning Finance and Economy Section, the Urban Lab, Urban Health and Human Rights and Social Inclusion Unit. The link of the project with UN-Habitat tools and how to mainstream in them sport and active recreation makes it very relevant for the value proposition of UN-Habitat, linking with aspects of inclusion, public space, services and regeneration (SP1, local economic development and creative industries (SP2), climate adaptation and mitigation (SP3) and integration of migrants and refugee communities through sport (SP4). The value-add results from the linkage between sports, active recreation and urban development (and its aspects of inclusion, sustainability and resilience). By combining sports with UN-Habitat's focus on urbanization, the transformative power of sports is utilized to enhance community engagement, inclusive communities, quality public space, adequate housing, sustainable mobility, urban health, air quality, urban regeneration, climate change adaptation and integration of vulnerable groups including migrants, refugees and IDPs.
Equally, there has been broad recognition of the potential for sport, physical activity and active recreation to be a catalyst for inclusive sustainable development, including explicit acknowledgement of “an important enabler of sustainable development” in the 2030 Agenda. There is also a growing evidence base on the value and social return of safe, inclusive and sustainable sport-based investments that are development-orientated and intentionally designed. These frameworks recognise that as well as sport being an important driver of Good Health and Wellbeing (SDG 3), well designed and intentionally-delivered sport policies and programmes can play an important role in championing Gender Equality (SDG 5), Decent Work and Economic Growth (SDG 8), Reduced Inequalities (SDG 10), Sustainable Cities and Communities (SDG 11), Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions (SDG 16) and Partnerships for the Goals (SDG 17) as elaborated below.
In turn the IOC’s strategic road map, Olympic Agenda 2020+5 sets out among its priorities strengthening the role of sport as an enabler of sustainable development. This roadmap also prioritises the promotion of urban sports and supporting a more diverse range of cities to benefit from hosting sporting events on the Road to the Olympic Games, which are also relevant to the wider New Urban Agenda.
